title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: up to 100 review sets per case (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: The briefing passes: the launched government-cloud limit increase matches the roadmap, and Microsoft Learn supports the limits, licensing, storage behaviour and documented controls. The page also reports the conflicting Microsoft descriptions of the premium case toggle rather than silently choosing one.

claims.where: What's changing; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The published premium case limit is 40 million documents across all review sets.
claims.quote: | Total number of documents that you can add to a case (for all review sets in a case). | 40 million |

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Adding collected content to a review set copies it from the original content location.
claims.quote: All items in the search results are copied from the original data source in the live services to a secure Azure Storage location in the Microsoft cloud.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Cost and licensing; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Review set content is held in Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed Azure Storage.
claims.quote: | Is review set content stored in Microsoft-managed Azure Storage? | Yes. The storage is Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed. Customers don't see, manage, or pay for these storage resources directly. |

claims.claim: Review set items and metadata are copied to storage dedicated to the case.
claims.quote: When you add content to a review set, the items and their metadata are copied to a Microsoft-managed Azure Storage location dedicated to the case.

claims.claim: Storage is provisioned per case and shared by its review sets.
claims.quote: Storage is provisioned **per case**. Multiple review sets within the same case share the underlying case storage, with logical separation so each review set's content remains independently queryable, taggable, and exportable.

claims.claim: Investigators can search review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Investigators can filter review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Investigators can tag review set content.
claims.quote: Review sets provide a static, known set of content that you can search, filter, tag, analyze, and predict relevancy using predictive coding models.

claims.claim: Investigators can export review set content.
claims.quote: After the review set processing completes, select the **Review sets** tab in the case, then select the review set to start the process of filtering, reviewing, tagging, and exporting data in the review set.

claims.claim: Customer Key encrypts review set content at rest with the customer-managed key when the tenant is configured with Customer Key.
claims.quote: Yes. If your tenant is configured with [Customer Key](/en-us/purview/customer-key-overview), review set content at rest is encrypted with the customer-managed key.

claims.claim: Customers do not directly see, manage or pay for the review set storage resources.
claims.quote: The storage is Microsoft-owned and Microsoft-managed. Customers don't see, manage, or pay for these storage resources directly.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing; Scope; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Learn says organisations with Office 365 E5, Microsoft 365 E5 or related E5 add-on subscriptions can use premium eDiscovery features.
claims.quote: If your organization has an Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5 subscription (or related E5 add-on subscriptions), you can further manage cases and analyze content by using premium eDiscovery features.

claims.claim: The higher review set ceiling is included within the licence entitlement to premium eDiscovery.

claims.claim: No administrator activation step is documented specifically for the increase to 100 review sets.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery review sets limit 100 increase automatic enable administrator switch 560322; "eDiscovery" "review set limit" "enable" "100". Opened edisc-ref-limits, edisc-settings-cases and edisc-settings-general; read both roadmap records.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters
claims.claim: The launched increase raises the ceiling for cases with premium features without a separate opt-in to the limit increase.
claims.quote: "status": "Launched"; "description": "Review set limit per case is increased from 20 per case to 100 per case."

claims.claim: The Purview permission assignment path is Settings > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > eDiscovery Manager > Edit > Manage eDiscovery Manager > Choose users.
claims.quote: Go to **Settings** > **Role groups**. On **Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions**, select **eDiscovery Manager**. Select **Edit**. On **Manage eDiscovery Manager**, select **Choose users** or **Choose groups**.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group> adds a security group to the eDiscovery Manager role group.
claims.quote: Add-RoleGroupMember "eDiscoveryManager" -Member <name of security group>

claims.claim: This command uses Security & Compliance PowerShell and adds a mail-enabled security group to the eDiscovery Managers subgroup.
claims.quote: You can add a mail-enabled security group as a member of the eDiscovery Managers subgroup in the *eDiscovery Manager* role group by using the **Add-RoleGroupMember** cmdlet in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].governs; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: eDiscovery Manager role group membership governs the ability to create cases and work with their review sets.
claims.quote: Members can also create and manage cases, add, and remove users for a case, create case holds, run searches associated with a case, and access case data.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Manager can access review sets in cases they create and are members of.
claims.quote: **eDiscovery Manager**. Allows members to access review sets in eDiscovery cases they create and are members of.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can access review sets in all cases.
claims.quote: **eDiscovery Administrator**. Provides all the permissions of eDiscovery Manager, plus the ability to access review sets in all eDiscovery cases in the organization.

claims.claim: A Reviewer can view documents in review sets in cases where they are a member.
claims.quote: **Reviewer**. Provides read-only access to review sets within eDiscovery cases where the user is a member. Reviewers can view and tag documents but cannot perform other case management tasks.

claims.claim: A Reviewer can tag documents in review sets in cases where they are a member.
claims.quote: **Reviewer**. Provides read-only access to review sets within eDiscovery cases where the user is a member. Reviewers can view and tag documents but cannot perform other case management tasks.

claims.claim: A Reviewer cannot perform other case management tasks.
claims.quote: Reviewers can view and tag documents but cannot perform other case management tasks.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Manager can manage only cases they create.
claims.quote: eDiscovery Managers can only access and manage the cases they create. They can't access or manage cases created by other eDiscovery Managers.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can access all cases.
claims.quote: Access all cases that are listed on the **eDiscovery** area in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can configure eDiscovery solution settings.
claims.quote: Configure eDiscovery solution settings.

claims.claim: An eDiscovery Administrator can manage any case after adding themselves as a member.
claims.quote: Manage any eDiscovery case after they add themselves as a member of the case.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The premium case toggle is in Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Premium features > eDiscovery (Premium).
claims.quote: Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, then select **Cases** in the left navigation. Select a case, then select **Case settings**. **Premium features**: ... turn on the **eDiscovery (Premium)** toggle.

claims.claim: PATCH /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/settings updates the case settings, including caseType.
claims.quote: PATCH /security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/settings; caseType ... The type of the eDiscovery case. The possible values are: `standard`, `premium`, `unknownFutureValue`.

claims.claim: The deciding request-body property is caseType, which accepts standard or premium.
claims.quote: | caseType | ... | The type of the eDiscovery case. The possible values are: `standard`, `premium`, `unknownFutureValue`. |

claims.claim: The case settings documentation says premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access.
claims.quote: Premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access.

claims.claim: The case settings documentation says premium features can be turned off per case after creation.
claims.quote: Premium features are enabled by default for tenants with premium feature access. To turn off, toggle the setting after a case is created.

claims.claim: The cases dashboard page gives the conflicting statement that access to premium features is not governed by the case settings toggle.
claims.quote: All cases created in the Microsoft Purview portal are the *Premium* type, regardless of your license or subscription. Access to premium features isn't governed by the case settings toggle.

claims.where: controls[2].ui; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls table
claims.claim: A new review set can be created at eDiscovery > Cases > case > Searches > search > Add to review set > Add items to review set > Add to a new review set in the Purview portal.
claims.quote: Select a search on the **Searches** tab, and then select **Add to review set**. On the **Add items to review set** flyout, select **Add to a new review set** or **Add to an existing review set**.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: POST /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId}/reviewSets creates a new review set.
claims.quote: Create a new [ediscoveryReviewSet] object. POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/b0073e4e-4184-41c6-9eb7-8c8cc3e2288b/reviewSets

claims.claim: The Microsoft Graph create reviewSets operation supports application permissions.
claims.quote: | Application | eDiscovery.Read.All | eDiscovery.ReadWrite.All |

claims.claim: For delegated access, the Graph operations shown require a signed-in user assigned a supported Purview eDiscovery role.
claims.quote: For delegated access using work or school accounts, the signed-in user must be assigned a supported [Microsoft Purview role] through one of the following options:

claims.claim: eDiscovery Manager is the least privileged documented option for accessing review sets in the user's own cases.
claims.quote: **eDiscovery Manager**. Allows members to access review sets in eDiscovery cases they create and are members of. **This is the least privileged option for accessing review sets in their own cases**.

claims.claim: The Purview case deletion path is eDiscovery > Cases > case > Case settings > Actions > Delete case.
claims.quote: Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, then select **Cases** in the left navigation. Select a case, then select **Case settings**. On the **Case settings** page, select **Actions**, then select **Delete case**.

claims.claim: DELETE /v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/{ediscoveryCaseId} deletes the case and thereby its review sets.
claims.quote: Delete an [ediscoveryCase] object. DELETE https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/security/cases/ediscoveryCases/22aa2acd-7554-4330-9ba9-ce20014aaae4

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: In data spillage scenarios, deleting the case is the only documented way to remove items from its review sets.
claims.quote: In data spillage scenarios, the only way to remove items in a review set is to delete the eDiscovery case. Other search and purge methods don't remove items from a review set.

claims.claim: Deleting a case deletes its searches, review sets and exports.
claims.quote: When you delete a case, you also delete all components associated with the case, such as the list of communications, searches, review sets, and exports.

claims.claim: Case deletion cannot be undone.
claims.quote: You can't recover or reopen a deleted case.

claims.where: controls[3].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: All case hold policies, including those with status Off, must be deleted before the case can be deleted.
claims.quote: Before you can delete a case, you must delete *all* hold policies listed on the **Hold policies** tab of the case. This requirement includes deleting holds with a status of **Off**.

claims.claim: The tenant default for new cases is configured at Microsoft Purview portal > eDiscovery > Settings > eDiscovery > General > eDiscovery (Premium).
claims.quote: Select the **eDiscovery** solution card, then go to **Settings** > **eDiscovery** > **General**. Select or clear the toggle for **eDiscovery (Premium)**.

claims.claim: Only eDiscovery Administrators can access the general premium default setting.
claims.quote: Only users assigned to the eDiscovery *Administrators* role can access this setting.

claims.claim: Changing the general premium setting affects new cases only, not existing cases.
claims.quote: Enabling premium eDiscovery features only affects new cases and doesn't affect the license state of any existing cases.

claims.claim: A case groups investigation searches, holds and review sets under case membership that controls access to its contents.
claims.quote: An eDiscovery [case] contains all searches, holds, and review sets related to a specific investigation. You can also assign members to a case to control who can access the case and view the contents of the case.
